jobs.name: Hermes backup
jobs.prompt: Run the Hermes backup script and publish the library. Output is the script's own stdout.

jobs.name: Weekly whereabouts note
jobs.prompt:
Build this week's TRIBE whereabouts note. Draft only: there is no sending step, and you must not send, schedule or forward any email.

1. Work in /Users/samuelkn/tribe-hermes-library. In apps/team-map run:
   python3 make_week.py --xlsx "$HOME/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-TribeTravelandEvents/TRIBE GROUP - Share Drive/Leave Calendar 2026.xlsx" --week <today's date YYYY-MM-DD>
   That writes apps/team-map/weeks/<monday>/ with data.json, data.js, map.html, map.png and email.html.
2. Capture the map: open weeks/<monday>/map.html in the browser, wait for window.__mapReady, set the viewport to 1060 wide at device scale 2, hide the h1, then screenshot the .stage element down to the last face in #unplaced, and save it as weeks/<monday>/map.png.
3. Run python3 publish.py --week <monday>. It copies the map to the TRIBE GROUP site under TRIBE Group Tech/Whereabouts/<monday>/ and writes that address into email.html. Open the printed link while signed in and confirm the image loads.
4. Read the rendered pin labels back out of the DOM and check the email: first names only, the base city carries a count, a trip carries names, anyone with no recorded place appears as a face under the map. Compare against data.json.
5. Run python3 scripts/hermes_files.py sync from the repo root so templates and generators publish. The generated week folder and the Whereabouts copies must not go into git or the Hermes Library.
6. Report, in plain prose: the folder path, the SharePoint link, the pins with their counts and names, who is away with no location, and any event in the workflow sheet the run could not place. If the workflow sheet or the leave calendar is missing or renamed, say so plainly instead of guessing.

Context you cannot see: the leave calendar lives in the Share Drive as 'Leave Calendar' with a year in the name. Work places come from the newest Workflow_*.xlsx in Share Drive/WORKFLOW, matched by the Onsite column's initials. where.json holds only overrides: site visits and shared holidays. Fridays default to work from home unless the calendar says otherwise. Leave data is private: never put the generated week folder in the shared library or in git. The note carries the map inline so it renders everywhere, plus the SharePoint link for full size.
